                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'## Service-to-Service Calls\n'[39m +

                      [32m'package order\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"context"\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining Type-Safe APIs - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-28, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API, add the `//encore:api` annotation to a function in your code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This tells Encore that the function is an API endpoint and Encore will REDACTEDmatically generate the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the example below, we define the API endpoint `Ping`, in the `hello` service, which gets exposed as `hello.Ping`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package hello // service name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Ping(ctx context.Context, params *PingParams) (*PingResponse, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'msg := fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", params.Name)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return &PingResponse{Message: msg}, nil\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Ping(ctx context.Context, params *PingParams) (*PingResponse, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'msg := fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", params.Name)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'oldRouter *gin.Engine // existing HTTP router\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func (s *Service) Fallback(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m's.oldRouter.ServeHTTP(w, req)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a REST API, start by defining an endpoint and specify the `method` and `path` fields in the `//encore:api` comment.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# LLM Instruction for Encore TypeScript Backend Framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-28, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://gist.github.com/qhoirulanwar/dedb31c00eb1aa8c86005f17c6c30023)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the `//encore:api` annotation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'When you use a struct type as the last argument in the function signature,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a REST API, start by defining an endpoint and specify the `method` and `path` fields in the `//encore:api` comment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction to Path and Query Parameters in Go | CodeSignal Learn\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-03-05, [Read more](https://codesignal.com/learn/courses/basics-of-http-requests-with-go/lessons/introduction-to-path-and-query-parameters-in-go)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are part of the URL used to access specific resources within an API, acting like unique identifiers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, if you want to retrieve a to-do item with ID `3`, the URL would be structured as follows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, `3` is the path parameter specifying the particular item you wish to access.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Fetching Data with Path Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are used to target specific resources within an API, allowing you to access individual items directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'They are appended directly to the endpoint URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For instance, if you want to fetch details of a specific to-do item using its ID, you'd use a path parameter.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Here's a practical example using ID `3`:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'In this example, `todoID` is a path parameter specifying the to-do item with ID `3`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If successful, the function prints the details of that specific item.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This demonstrates how path parameters enable you to access individual resources accurately.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this lesson, you’ve learned how to work with both path and query parameters to refine API requests in Go.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters allow you to pinpoint specific resources, whereas query parameters tailor the results based on defined conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Together, they provide a robust mechanism for fetching targeted and detailed information from an API.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vanilla GO Path Parameters - JonathanMH\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-13, last updated: 2026-03-12, [Read more](https://jonathanmh.com/p/vanilla-go-path-parameters/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Golang introduced easier path parameter based routing as a vanilla language feature with the 1.22 release, which is incredibly handy if you don't have a lot of routes or if a generic http framework does not make sense for your use case.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So if I want to see my signed up users I would issue a GET request to `/users` and if I want to see a specific user I would do the same with `/users/1`, the `1` being the relevant path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So far so good, we have a web server and now we want to add a route for the users with a dynamic path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next we need to add a new route that specifies the `{id}` as a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'mux.HandleFunc("/hello-world", helloHandler)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'+ mux.HandleFunc("/users/{id}", userHandler)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func userHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userId := r.PathValue("id")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fmt.Println("got userId:", userId)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To retrieve the path parameter value we use `userId := r.PathValue("id")`, which needs to specify the same string that we defined in the route (`{id}`) omitting the curly braces.'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Metadata API – Get data about apps, envs, and requests\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-09-08, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/develop/metadata)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore.CurrentRequest()` can be called from anywhere within your application and will return an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore.Request instance which will provides information about why the current\n'[39m +
                      [32m'code is running.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The encore.Request type contains information about the running request, such as:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The service and endpoint being called\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Path and path parameter information\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- When the request started\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This works REDACTEDmatically as a result of Encore's request tracking, and works even in other goroutines that were spawned\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be useful on raw endpoints with path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'as the standard\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`http.Request` object passed into the raw endpoint does not provide access to the parsed path parameters,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'however by calling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore.CurrentRequest().PathParams()` you can get access to the parsed path parameters.'[39m

                      [32m'or by setting an environment variable at runtime.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A module is a collection of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Go packages stored in a file tree with a `go.mod` file at its root.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `go.mod` file defines the module’s *module path*, which is also the import path used for the root directory, and its *dependency requirements*, which are the other modules needed for a successful build.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Packages in subdirectories have import paths consisting of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the module path plus the path to the subdirectory.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `go` command resolves imports by using the specific\n'[39m +
                      [32m'dependency module versions listed in `go.mod`.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Git error: "Host Key Verification Failed" when connecting to remote repository\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- I'm guessing the contents of your `known_hosts` file are bad.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It should be the host key, on one terribly long line.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you only have the host name there (for example) it will not work.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I recommend that you remove this file (if indeed it only contains the information for this single host) and allow SSH to create it next time you connect.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Add the following line to your ssh config file ($HOME/.ssh/config):\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'My solution was to manually fill `~/.ssh/known_hosts` with all the possible server names that Gridengine could choose (use `qhost` to list the servers):\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- copy content of id_rsa.pub (client) to file ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (server)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- chmod 700 ~/.ssh\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Managing Your SSH known_hosts Using Git - JamieWeb.net\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://www.jamieweb.net/blog/managing-your-ssh-known_hosts-using-git/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `known_hosts` file, normally located at `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, is used to store the SSH server key fingerprints of the servers that you have connected to in the past.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each SSH server has its own (normally unique) server key and associated fingerprint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The manual page explain the format in detail.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In order to actually acquire the fingerprint to add to the file, you can use the `ssh-keyscan` command.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Firstly, you'll need to tell SSH where your fingerprints are stored:** This can be done using the `UserKnownHostsFile` option in your local (or global if you want) SSH config.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`UserKnownHostsFile` is a space-separated list of paths to files containing valid fingerprints that SSH will use when connecting to servers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The first defined file is used as the main one, and is where new fingerprints will be saved to.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I prefer to use the default `~/.ssh/known_hosts` file as the main one, and then add the other files from the Git repository afterwards.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'UserKnownHostsFile ~/.ssh/known_hosts ~/jamieweb/known_hosts/ldn01/fingerprint\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Has GitHub changed his remote host key ? #50878\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's in\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~/.ssh/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m', where the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'stands for your home directory (where that is depends on your system).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, I think the old ECDSA RSA key for the github.com *IP* needs to be removed from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'known_hosts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. This can be done with:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ssh-keygen -f ~/.ssh/known_hosts -R GITHUB_IP_HERE\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"$ sed -i.github-removed '/AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAABIwAAAQEAq2A7hRGmdnm9tUDbO9IDSwBK6TbQa/d' ~/.ssh/known_hosts\n"[39m +
                      [32m"$ curl -L https://api.github.com/meta | jq -r '.ssh_keys | .[]' | sed -e 's/^/github.com /' >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The hostnames/IPs are hashed, not encrypted. Use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ssh-keygen -R\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'known_hosts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2023-10-11, last updated: 2026-04-18, [Read more](https://github.com/kubernetes/git-sync/issues/824)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'value: git@gitea-ssh.gitosis.svc.cluster.local:user/repo.git\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Can you run with `-v 9` and paste the `"starting up"` line (redacted as you see fit)?\n'[39m +

                      [32m'However, if I copy `/etc/git-secret/ssh` to `/root/.ssh/id_rsa` and `/etc/git-secret/known_hosts` to the same directory, the regular ssh client logs in accepting the host key as-is.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Git与SSH\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-06-22, [Read more](https://deepinout.com/git/git-questions/1206_git_git_says_warning_permanently_added_to_the_list_of_known_hosts.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'可以通过手动验证远程主机的公钥，并将其添加到”known_hosts”文件中，以消除这个警告。这可以通过使用命令行工具ssh-keyscan来完成。以下是使用ssh-keyscan的示例命令：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ ssh-keyscan <remote_host> >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Host <remote_host>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'StrictHostKeyChecking no\n'[39m +
                      [32m'UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'如果你认为”known_hosts”文件已经被损坏或包含错误的公钥信息，可以尝试清空该文件。这将导致Git在连接到新的主机时重新验证公钥并重新记录。以下是清空”known_hosts”文件的示例命令：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ > ~/.ssh/known_hosts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'上述命令将清空当前用户的”known_hosts”文件。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'首先，你可以使用以下命令获取远程主机A的公钥：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'With ``` -f ``` option, ``` git ``` ``` fetch ``` *<name>* is run immediately after the remote information is set up.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'You can give more than one ``` -t ``` *<branch>* to track multiple branches without grabbing all branches.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Change URLs for the remote.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Sets first URL for remote *<name>* that matches regex*<oldurl>*(first URL if no*<oldurl>* is given) to*<newurl>*.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - encoredev/git-remote-grpc: Clone git repositories over gRPC\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-03, [Read more](https://github.com/encoredev/git-remote-grpc)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This project provides sample code for building a git remote helper that allows for cloning, fetching, and pushing updates to remote git repositories over gRPC.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be really useful for leveraging existing gRPC infrastructure, such as TLS authentication support, to avoid having to build a separate Public Key Infrastructure for authenticating with SSH keys.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - parapluu/encore: The Encore compiler.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2014-04-14, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/parapluu/encore)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do this, add this line to your `~/.bashrc` file, inserting the proper path for `<SOME_DIR>`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export PATH="<SOME_DIR>/encore/release:${PATH}"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Simplify your backend with Git clone of gRPC - Encore.dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-05-10, last updated: 2025-09-16, [Read more](https://encore.dev/blog/git-clone-grpc)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Like many backends, Encore uses gRPC internally for cross-service communication.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This makes it trivial to do end-to-end authentication and encryption.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We really didn't want to build a whole separate authentication mechanism with SSH keys just to be able to interact with Git repositories.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In summary, when git encounters a remote URL called\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`<transport>://<address>` it looks for an executable\n'[39m +
                      [32m'named\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`git-remote-<transport>` on the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`$PATH`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It invokes it with either one or two arguments,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'where the first argument is the remote name (if available), and the second argument is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`<address>` (if available).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for connecting to the remote server and invoking either git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack on the remote end, and connect them to stdin and stdout\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So with this functionality we can now build our own\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`git-remote-grpc` executable that communicates over gRPC.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`connect` function is responsible for parsing the remote address, establishing a gRPC connection,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and proxying stdin/stdout data over the connection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// If testing locally without TLS certificates, you can add grpc.WithInsecure() to bypass TLS.'[39m

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +

You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills below can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The only thing you need to do is import the service you want to call from `~encore/clients` and then call its API endpoints like functions.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining Type-Safe APIs - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-28, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API, add the `//encore:api` annotation to a function in your code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This tells Encore that the function is an API endpoint and Encore will REDACTEDmatically generate the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package hello // service name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Ping(ctx context.Context, params *PingParams) (*PingResponse, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'msg := fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", params.Name)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return &PingResponse{Message: msg}, nil\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Ping(ctx context.Context, params *PingParams) (*PingResponse, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'msg := fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", params.Name)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore.dev - Go Packages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-10, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/encore.dev)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### type PathParam ¶\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type PathParam struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Name string // the name of the path parameter, without leading ':' or '*'.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Value string // the parsed path parameter value.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PathParam represents a parsed path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### type PathParams ¶\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type PathParams []PathParam\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PathParams contains the path parameters parsed from the request path.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The ordering of the parameters in the path will be maintained from the URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### func (PathParams) Get ¶\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func (PathParams) Get(name string) (_ string)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Get returns the value of the path parameter with the given name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If no such parameter exists it reports "".\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining Type-Safe APIs - Encore.dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-28, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the `//encore:api` annotation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore parses the incoming request URL and makes sure it matches the type of the parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The last segment of the path\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can be parsed as a wildcard parameter by using `*name` with a matching function parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you use a struct type as the last argument in the function signature,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a REST API, start by defining an endpoint and specify the `method` and `path` fields in the `//encore:api` comment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also combine path parameters with body payloads.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You cannot define paths that conflict with each other, including paths\n'[39m +
                      [32m'where the static part can be mistaken for a parameter, e.g both `/blog` and `/blog/:id` would conflict with `/:username`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As a rule of thumb, try to place path parameters at the end of the path and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'prefix them with the service name, e.g:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction to Path and Query Parameters in Go | CodeSignal Learn\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-03-05, [Read more](https://codesignal.com/learn/courses/basics-of-http-requests-with-go/lessons/introduction-to-path-and-query-parameters-in-go)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are part of the URL used to access specific resources within an API, acting like unique identifiers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, if you want to retrieve a to-do item with ID `3`, the URL would be structured as follows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, `3` is the path parameter specifying the particular item you wish to access.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Fetching Data with Path Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are used to target specific resources within an API, allowing you to access individual items directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'They are appended directly to the endpoint URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For instance, if you want to fetch details of a specific to-do item using its ID, you'd use a path parameter.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Here's a practical example using ID `3`:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'In this example, `todoID` is a path parameter specifying the to-do item with ID `3`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If successful, the function prints the details of that specific item.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This demonstrates how path parameters enable you to access individual resources accurately.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this lesson, you’ve learned how to work with both path and query parameters to refine API requests in Go.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters allow you to pinpoint specific resources, whereas query parameters tailor the results based on defined conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Together, they provide a robust mechanism for fetching targeted and detailed information from an API.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Getting Started with Encore.go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-26, last updated: 2025-10-07, [Read more](https://dev.to/eminetto/getting-started-with-encorego-3pk2)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// AuthParams are the parameters to the Auth method\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type AuthParams struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Email string `json:"email"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ValidateTokenParams are the parameters to the ValidateToken method\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type ValidateTokenParams struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Token string `json:"token"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type ValidateTokenResponse struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This declaration tells the framework that this is a public API (we'll see more about this in the following parts of this series) whose path is\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'/v1/auth\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and that it will be accessed via the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'POST\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An API is a function that receives a context and a parameter struct (in this case,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'AuthParams\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m').\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One of the interesting features of the framework is the ease of accessing the parameter values: we can use the values ​​as\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'p.Email\n'[39m +

                      [32m'11:07AM INF registered API endpoint endpoint=Auth path=/v1/auth service=user\n'[39m +
                      [32m'11:07AM INF registered API endpoint endpoint=ValidateToken path=/v1/validate-token service=user'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Quick Start Guide\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-31, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/quick-start)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public path=/hello/:name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func World(ctx context.Context, name string) (*Response, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'msg := "Hello, " + name + "!"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return &Response{Message: msg}, nil\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One such element is the API annotation:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public path=/hello/:name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vanilla GO Path Parameters - JonathanMH\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-13, last updated: 2026-03-12, [Read more](https://jonathanmh.com/p/vanilla-go-path-parameters/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Golang introduced easier path parameter based routing as a vanilla language feature with the 1.22 release, which is incredibly handy if you don't have a lot of routes or if a generic http framework does not make sense for your use case.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So if I want to see my signed up users I would issue a GET request to `/users` and if I want to see a specific user I would do the same with `/users/1`, the `1` being the relevant path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So far so good, we have a web server and now we want to add a route for the users with a dynamic path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next we need to add a new route that specifies the `{id}` as a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'mux.HandleFunc("/hello-world", helloHandler)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'+ mux.HandleFunc("/users/{id}", userHandler)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func userHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userId := r.PathValue("id")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fmt.Println("got userId:", userId)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To retrieve the path parameter value we use `userId := r.PathValue("id")`, which needs to specify the same string that we defined in the route (`{id}`) omitting the curly braces.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Metadata API – Get data about apps, envs, and requests\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-09-08, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/develop/metadata)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore.CurrentRequest()` can be called from anywhere within your application and will return an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore.Request instance which will provides information about why the current\n'[39m +
                      [32m'code is running.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The encore.Request type contains information about the running request, such as:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The service and endpoint being called\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Path and path parameter information\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- When the request started\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This works REDACTEDmatically as a result of Encore's request tracking, and works even in other goroutines that were spawned\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be useful on raw endpoints with path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'as the standard\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`http.Request` object passed into the raw endpoint does not provide access to the parsed path parameters,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'however by calling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore.CurrentRequest().PathParams()` you can get access to the parsed path parameters.'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Managing Your SSH known_hosts Using Git - JamieWeb.net\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `known_hosts` file, normally located at `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, is used to store the SSH server key fingerprints of the servers that you have connected to in the past.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each SSH server has its own (normally unique) server key and associated fingerprint.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Firstly, you'll need to tell SSH where your fingerprints are stored:** This can be done using the `UserKnownHostsFile` option in your local (or global if you want) SSH config.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`UserKnownHostsFile` is a space-separated list of paths to files containing valid fingerprints that SSH will use when connecting to servers.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'I prefer to use the default `~/.ssh/known_hosts` file as the main one, and then add the other files from the Git repository afterwards.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'UserKnownHostsFile ~/.ssh/known_hosts ~/jamieweb/known_hosts/ldn01/fingerprint\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, I think the old ECDSA RSA key for the github.com *IP* needs to be removed from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'known_hosts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. This can be done with:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ssh-keygen -f ~/.ssh/known_hosts -R GITHUB_IP_HERE\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m"$ curl -L https://api.github.com/meta | jq -r '.ssh_keys | .[]' | sed -e 's/^/github.com /' >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts\n"[39m +

                      [32m'The hostnames/IPs are hashed, not encrypted. Use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'可以通过手动验证远程主机的公钥，并将其添加到”known_hosts”文件中，以消除这个警告。这可以通过使用命令行工具ssh-keyscan来完成。以下是使用ssh-keyscan的示例命令：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Host <remote_host>\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'手动预加载目标主机的公钥到 `known_hosts`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'使用 `StrictHostKeyChecking` 和 `UserKnownHostsFile` 配置项控制 SSH 行为\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'在 CI/CD 环境中构建自定义镜像，预先信任目标主机\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- 4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'使用 HTTPS 协议代替 SSH 协议进行 Git 操作\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'通过 `ssh-keyscan` 工具可以获取远程主机的公钥并写入 `known_hosts` 文件，避免首次连接时出现提示。\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The command ``` git ``` ``` fetch ``` *<name>* can then be used to create and update remote-tracking branches*<name>* ``` / ``` *<branch>*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With ``` -f ``` option, ``` git ``` ``` fetch ``` *<name>* is run immediately after the remote information is set up.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore/CONTRIBUTING.md at main · encoredev/encore\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-02-17, last updated: 2025-02-11, [Read more](https://github.com/encoredev/encore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The easiest way to get started with developing Encore is using\n'[39m +
                      [32m'GitHub Codespaces.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Simply open this repository in a new Codespace\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and your development environment will be set up with everything preconfigured for building the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore` CLI and running applications with it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This also works just as well with Visual Studio Code's Remote Development.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'## Building the encore command from source\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To build from the source simply run\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`go build ./cli/cmd/encore` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`go install ./cli/cmd/git-remote-encore`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This must be set to the location of the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore.dev` runtime package.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's located in this Git repository in the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`runtimes` directory:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`export ENCORE_RUNTIMES_PATH=/path/to/encore/runtimes`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do that, run\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`encore daemon env` and grab the value of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`ENCORE_GOROOT`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example (yours is probably different):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`export ENCORE_GOROOT=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/encore/0.16.2/libexec/encore-go`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start the daemon with the built binary:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`./encore daemon -f`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encr.dev module - encr.dev - Go Packages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-19, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/encr.dev)\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Fix typos in comments and docs (#843) · encoredev/encore@0745a8d\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-08-10, last updated: 2025-07-03, [Read more](http://github.com/encoredev/encore/commit/0745a8dfdd98ae1432107b6af56c070c76f9bb81)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Step 4: Push to deploy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/platform/deploy/deploying)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Already created an application locally?\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Follow these steps if you've already created an app and want to link it to an account on Encore Cloud:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'**1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Ensure you are logged in with the CLI**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"encore auth signup # If you haven't created an Encore Cloud account\n"[39m +
                      [32m"encore auth login # If you've already created an Encore Cloud account\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Link your local app to Encore Cloud**\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Run this command from you application's root folder:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore app init\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Set up Encore's git remote to enable pushing directly to Encore Cloud**\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Run this command from you application's root folder:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'git remote add encore encore://<app-id>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Step 4: Push to deploy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Deploy your application by pushing your code to the connected Git repository.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Using Encore Cloud's managed git**:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ git add -A .\n'[39m +
                      [32m"$ git commit -m 'Commit message'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'$ git push encore\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **If you have connected your GitHub account:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ git add -A .\n'[39m +
                      [32m"$ git commit -m 'Commit message'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'$ git push origin\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - encoredev/git-remote-grpc: Clone git repositories over gRPC\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-03, [Read more](https://github.com/encoredev/git-remote-grpc)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This project provides sample code for building a git remote helper that allows for cloning, fetching, and pushing updates to remote git repositories over gRPC.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be really useful for leveraging existing gRPC infrastructure, such as TLS authentication support, to avoid having to build a separate Public Key Infrastructure for authenticating with SSH keys.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - parapluu/encore: The Encore compiler.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2014-04-14, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/parapluu/encore)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do this, add this line to your `~/.bashrc` file, inserting the proper path for `<SOME_DIR>`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export PATH="<SOME_DIR>/encore/release:${PATH}"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Simplify your backend with Git clone of gRPC - Encore.dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-05-10, last updated: 2025-09-16, [Read more](https://encore.dev/blog/git-clone-grpc)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Like many backends, Encore uses gRPC internally for cross-service communication.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This makes it trivial to do end-to-end authentication and encryption.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We really didn't want to build a whole separate authentication mechanism with SSH keys just to be able to interact with Git repositories.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In summary, when git encounters a remote URL called\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`<transport>://<address>` it looks for an executable\n'[39m +
                      [32m'named\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`git-remote-<transport>` on the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`$PATH`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It invokes it with either one or two arguments,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'where the first argument is the remote name (if available), and the second argument is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`<address>` (if available).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for connecting to the remote server and invoking either git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack on the remote end, and connect them to stdin and stdout\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So with this functionality we can now build our own\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`git-remote-grpc` executable that communicates over gRPC.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`connect` function is responsible for parsing the remote address, establishing a gRPC connection,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and proxying stdin/stdout data over the connection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// If testing locally without TLS certificates, you can add grpc.WithInsecure() to bypass TLS.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore.dev - Go Packages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-10, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/encore.dev)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This repository contains the Encore's Runtime API contract, which Encore applications are built against.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'go get -u encore.dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  }

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +

When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes.
